_about: Components worth preparing once for several upcoming meals. match is a regex on ingredient names (case-insensitive); skip excludes. unit grams convert counts and spoons. fridgeDays: how long the prepared component keeps in a fridge at 4 °C or colder; roomHours: how long it keeps at Bengaluru room temperature (0 = make it on the day it's cooked). Keeping times follow FoodSafety.gov / USDA cold-storage charts and the National Center for Home Food Preservation's guidance on garlic in oil; they are guidance, not guarantees.

sources.title: National Center for Home Food Preservation: garlic and herbs in oil must be refrigerated
USDA FSIS: leftovers and the 2-hour rule

components.title: Ginger-garlic paste
components.how: Peel equal weights of ginger and garlic, grind with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt per 50 g (water only if needed). Keep in a clean, dry glass jar.
components.noFridge: Homemade ginger-garlic paste must be refrigerated (garlic in oil is a botulism risk at room temperature). Without a fridge, crush only what today's cooking needs, or use a sealed shop-bought pack.

components.title: Peeled garlic cloves
components.how: Soak the bulbs 10 minutes in warm water and the skins slip off. Store peeled cloves dry in a closed jar.
components.noFridge: Peeled cloves keep about a day in a covered jar out of the sun. Peel tomorrow's too, no more.

components.title: Chopped or sliced onions
components.how: Chop or slice with the pull-cord chopper, then pack in an airtight box lined with a paper towel. Keep each recipe's share separate if they're cut differently.
components.noFridge: Cut onions spoil and smell quickly in the warm. Peel today, chop just before cooking; peeled whole onions keep a day in a closed box.

components.title: Tomato purée
components.how: Blanch or blend raw tomatoes to a purée and keep in a closed jar.

components.title: Chapati dough
components.how: Knead once for the next two days, rub with a little oil, and keep in a closed box. Bring it to room temperature 20 minutes before rolling.
components.noFridge: Dough keeps about 4 hours covered in a cool spot (it starts to sour after that). Knead in the morning for lunch, again in the evening for dinner.

components.title: Cooked beans and chana
components.match: rajma|kabuli chana|kala chana|alasande|dried green peas|horse gram|black-eyed
components.how: Pressure-cook the soaked beans for all the dishes together, cool them quickly in a wide bowl, and store with a little of their cooking water.
components.noFridge: Cook beans on the day you eat them.

components.title: Grated fresh coconut
components.how: Grate a whole coconut once and keep it in a closed box.
components.noFridge: Grated coconut sours within hours in the warm: grate it on the day, or keep the coconut halves whole until you need them.

components.title: Dry-roasted rava
components.how: Dry-roast rava on low heat 6–8 minutes until it smells toasty and flows freely, cool completely and store airtight. Upma and kesari then skip the roasting step.
components.noFridge: Keeps for weeks in an airtight tin: no fridge needed.

components.title: Roasted peanuts
components.how: Dry-roast on low until the skins crack (8–10 minutes) or air-fry at 160 °C for 8 minutes. Cool fully before closing the jar.
components.noFridge: Keeps about 2 weeks in an airtight jar: no fridge needed.

components.title: Tamarind extract
components.how: Soak a lemon-sized ball in ¾ cup hot water for 15 minutes, squeeze, strain and keep in a jar.
components.noFridge: Soak tamarind just before cooking (15 minutes); the dry block itself keeps for months.

noFridge: Cook close to eating time. Cooked food can stay out at most 2 hours (1 hour on a hot day); after that keep it piping hot or throw it away.
Rice is the riskiest leftover: cook it just before the meal and don't keep any.
Buy milk, curd, paneer and chicken on the day you use them. Boil milk morning and night so it lasts the day.
Marinate meat for at most 2 hours, covered, in the coolest spot, then cook it.
Soak beans in a cool corner, covered; change the water once if they soak more than 8 hours.
Batch the dry work instead: roast rava and peanuts, make chutney pudi or podi, peel garlic and onions for today.
newFridge: When the new fridge arrives, let it run empty until it is properly cold (usually 2–4 hours; check its manual) before you load food. Then batch for the next three days.
